When hero beauty matters to the creator, commission or generate a visual prototype first and approve that target before producing the cast. This exposes the fidelity gap early rather than after the production style is locked.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Fortal XR dev guide: WebXR Quest MR rules, safety, comfort, performance

nodes.title: Make every strike produce local hit feedback
nodes.text: Every object that can be struck should support a visible emissive flash, with independently controllable materials whenever characters must react separately. Shared materials can otherwise make several characters flash as one and blur which target was hit. A brief flash on the struck character gives immediate, local confirmation without adding extra UI.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Fortal XR dev guide: WebXR Quest MR rules, safety, comfort, performance

nodes.title: Hand over headset evidence, not assumed readiness
nodes.text: With each headset prototype, provide a link that works on the target device, step-by-step controls, captures from the running build, and fps, draw-call and triangle figures when available. State plainly what has and has not been tested in the headset. A localhost link only works on the host computer, so headset review needs a deployed link.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Fortal XR dev guide: WebXR Quest MR rules, safety, comfort, performance

nodes.title: Echo player mistakes on the spectator display
nodes.text: Give spectators a dedicated visual reaction when a player triggers an important event, such as a glass ornament shattering when that player breaks a floor cell. Keep the effect decorative so it cannot alter gameplay, and make it brief and readable: shards can fall for 0.7 seconds and travel 0.6 metres before a fresh ornament appears after 1.5 seconds. Varying the motion and which ornament reacts keeps repeated events lively while preserving the cause-and-effect link.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Deepspace: Unity LED floor + UWB tracking game project

nodes.title: Use short rounds with explicit breathers
nodes.text: For an active group score chase, start from 3 rounds of 60 seconds, an 8 second break between rounds, and a 3 second countdown before play. The breaks create a clear rhythm for checking scores and recovering without ending the session, while the countdown prevents a confusing start. Treat these as playtest defaults rather than fixed rules.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Deepspace: Unity LED floor + UWB tracking game project

nodes.title: Align reward tiers with rarity and celebrate real pickups
nodes.text: Make value readable through a consistent visual ladder: in this design, six common bounties score 1 point, while the rarer most-wanted target scores 5. Bronze marks common rewards, silver the temporarily enlarged reward, and gold the rarest and most valuable. Play the coin-flip celebration only when a player actually collects a reward, not when it expires or is cleared, so the effect confirms player success rather than visual noise.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Deepspace: Unity LED floor + UWB tracking game project

nodes.title: Space pickups beyond double their collection reach
nodes.text: For position-based collection, keep item centres farther apart than twice the combined grab reach, or one standing position may collect two items. With a combined reach of 0.62 m, the danger threshold is 1.24 m: a 1.2 m minimum gap caused accidental double pickups, while 1.6 m provided reliable separation. Use the same reach-plus-margin calculation whenever spawn spacing is tuned.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Deepspace: Unity LED floor + UWB tracking game project

nodes.title: Give every input path the same brief button punch
nodes.text: Use one button-feedback pattern whether activation comes from a mouse, LED floor, or another input route. A useful tuning is a 0.15 scale punch over 0.25 seconds with vibrato 6, returning automatically to the original scale so Start, Restart, and Exit remain pressable. If a button also has an idle breathing pulse, suspend and restart that pulse around the punch instead of letting both animations fight over scale.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Deepspace: Unity LED floor + UWB tracking game project

nodes.title: Make tracked movement stable before tying gameplay to it
nodes.text: For a floor-positioned MR game, treat live positions as noisy: smooth the signal, ignore movements below about 0.03 m, and start with roughly 0.15 s of smoothing to reduce visible jitter. Reject implausible jumps and poses outside calibrated bounds, hold the last good position during brief signal gaps, then recover gradually rather than teleporting; useful starting limits are a 1 s pose age, 1 m bounds margin, and 2 m snap threshold. Playtest walking, stopping, and tracking loss, since sliding or sudden corrections can make checkpoint and hazard outcomes feel unfair.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Deepspace: Unity LED floor + UWB tracking game project

nodes.title: Handle tracked player loss without breaking the group
nodes.text: Give each of the 2 to 4 players a stable slot and an explicit measured, predicted, or lost state with an input age. When tracking is lost, stop that player's ready state, cursor, answers, and attacks without pausing or reassigning everyone else; on recovery, require fresh input rather than replaying stale actions. Never let bots silently replace real tracking, and reset readiness and session state between rounds.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Deepspace: Unity LED floor + UWB tracking game project

nodes.title: Make every supported player count a complete game
nodes.text: For selectable 2, 3, or 4 player sessions, build menus, playfields, and results from the chosen roster instead of discovering whoever happens to be in the scene. Check that every active player has an independent cursor, score, hit or answer grading, and a way to win or tie, while unused slots stay excluded. Use count dependent layouts and explicit physical progress units, for example two lanes per player in a path game, so adding players does not merely squeeze a two player screen.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Deepspace: Unity LED floor + UWB tracking game project

nodes.title: Prove physical tracking separately from gameplay
nodes.text: Prototype a tracked floor game with known metre points at the centre and corners, then test dropouts, long stalls, implausible jumps, and one tag disappearing while the others keep moving. Replay the same recorded cases before changing smoothing or jump thresholds, and keep prediction bounded. Mouse or bot play can validate menus and UI, and synthetic geometry can validate mapping, but neither proves real radio tracking accuracy.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Deepspace: Unity LED floor + UWB tracking game project

nodes.title: Use an automatic Ready-to-countdown onboarding beat
nodes.text: When players cannot pause with a keyboard, let the start press open a short Ready hold, then begin the 3-2-1 countdown automatically rather than chaining straight into play. Keep every in-round instruction, including Ready and prompts such as Walk, in one consistent headline position, and reveal hidden solution information only when the Memorize phase actually starts. This gives players a predictable moment to orient themselves without letting them study the answer early.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Deepspace: Unity LED floor + UWB tracking game project

nodes.title: Finish outcome effects before the judging beat ends
nodes.text: Budget the complete failure or success animation inside the state that displays it: in this project, all crack and shard runtime had to stay comfortably below the 1.3 second judging window. Do not merely start an effect at judgment and advance the state machine on a fixed timer, or the transition will cut it off. Treat the judging duration as an audiovisual budget and shorten or simplify effects when necessary.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Deepspace: Unity LED floor + UWB tracking game project

nodes.title: Separate player identity, game state, and surface decoration
nodes.text: Give each player a hollow ring with a solid inner circle, and reuse that player's inner-circle color in their progress display so identity remains consistent across the HUD. On grid cells, place beveled borders and gloss beneath a live gameplay tint for hidden, safe, breaking, broken, or wrong states. Decoration can make surfaces feel like glass, but the state color must remain the top readability layer.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Deepspace: Unity LED floor + UWB tracking game project

nodes.title: Keep MR sword combat grounded and visually clear
nodes.text: For an MR battle, make the right controller the sword: a fast swing attacks, real steps dodge red danger rings, and the trigger restarts after a run. Place the arena beneath the player's feet and align it with their initial view so the goal is immediately understandable. Hide tall decorative objects such as pillars and thrones in MR, leaving the floor and enemies readable against passthrough surroundings.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC battle engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Escalate a battle boss without losing dodge readability
nodes.text: Give the boss a clear targeted ground slam, then intensify the same pattern below half health by adding 3 extra warning rings and summoning weak grunts. This creates a readable second phase: the player already understands the main threat, while added rings test positioning and grunts divide attention. Keep the new pressure telegraphed rather than introducing an unrelated surprise attack.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC battle engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Make battle defense readable on the ground
nodes.text: Build PC sword combat around a 3-hit combo whose third strike deals double damage, plus a dash on Space or right click that evades attacks. Telegraph danger with red circles on the floor, and treat the circle's flash as the deadline: players must leave before it flashes. Introduce these two verbs in a low-pressure opening so later difficulty tests timing and positioning rather than control discovery.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC battle engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Escalate chapters before the boss
nodes.text: Give each battle chapter a title, one story line, and a bounded enemy wave, with at most 6 enemies of each kind per chapter. Escalate by changing the mix of fast grunts, front-blocking shields, and charging beasts rather than only adding bodies. Use rain as an optional pressure layer of continuously falling red warning rings, then end with the boss chapter, which the engine adds automatically as "Face <boss name>".
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC battle engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Anchor MR sword combat to the body and real floor
nodes.text: Treat MR battle as a room-scale, embodied encounter: the player's head position is the hero, and the right controller is the sword. Size the arena in metres for the available MR floor instead of reusing a PC arena, then arrange enemies and dodge room around that physical space. Quest 3 passthrough with a local-floor reference keeps combat anchored to the real surroundings.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC battle engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Make enemy roles readable through behavior and telegraphs
nodes.text: Build each enemy around a clear loop of entering, chasing, winding up, striking, and causing knockback, with a hit flash confirming successful attacks. Give large foes a visible wind-up ring before they swing, and reserve abrupt bursts for special roles such as a beast charging at 3.4 times its normal speed. Separate hp, speed, body radius, attack reach, wind-up time, damage, score, and size so roles can be tuned without changing their basic behavior.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC battle engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Pair combat stats with distinct silhouettes and independent flash materials
nodes.text: Give enemy kinds immediately different silhouettes, such as a humanoid skeleton, a front-facing shield-bearer, a broad four-legged beast, and a crowned boss. Size and posture should communicate threat before the player reads the HUD, while each model needs its own materials so a hit flash affects that enemy without changing the others. Treat visual identity and combat stats as one role-definition pass rather than decorating enemies after tuning.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC battle engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Start desktop melee movement at 5.2 metres per second
nodes.text: For a third-person desktop sword game, 5.2 m/s is a concrete starting run speed for WASD movement with mouse aim. Keep swing, combo window, dash, dash cooldown, invulnerability, and general cooldown as separate timers so responsiveness and punishment can be adjusted independently. Playtest whether players can reposition during enemy wind-ups before increasing enemy speed or damage.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC battle engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Give battle states distinct HUD homes
nodes.text: Separate persistent status from event feedback: health pips, score and clock stay visible, while chapter title and progress steps explain the current objective. Reserve the boss bar for the boss, a centre message for major prompts, and a hurt flash for damage; use start and end cards to frame play rather than crowding the arena.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC battle engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Fill warning rings before area strikes
nodes.text: Telegraph every area attack with a red floor circle that visibly fills before striking everything inside, so the fill is the player's dodge timer. Reuse the same readable language for cursed rain chapters, where multiple warning rings fall from the sky, and clear the rings when the encounter resets.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC battle engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Use chapter rewards to sustain battle tempo
nodes.text: Start battle scoring at 10 points per hit, with enemy kill values defined per enemy kind, then award 200 points and heal 2 health on each chapter clear. At victory, add bonuses for time left and remaining health at 100 points per health point; this makes clean play and efficient clears matter without requiring an inventory or upgrade system.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC battle engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Spawn enemies away from the player with a grow-in
nodes.text: Place ordinary enemies on an elliptical ring about 7 metres across in X and 5 metres in Z, away from the player, and place the king at the throne end for a deliberate boss entrance. A grow-in burst makes a new arrival legible before contact; small coloured tetrahedra with gravity, floor bounces and fading can also punctuate hits without persistent visual clutter.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC battle engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Tune tactics boards with small, legible budgets
nodes.text: Choose the player's movement identity first: knight, bishop, rook, or queen. A useful board budget is 2 to 6 ordered targets, 0 to 4 patrolling guards, 0 to 4 blocking tables, and 0 to 4 damaging cracked squares, with enemy movement every 1.5 to 3.5 seconds. Raise difficulty through route planning and patrol timing rather than filling every budget at once.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC tactics engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Prove ordered routes and a safe opening
nodes.text: Validate each board using the actual movement rules of its piece, checking that the player can reach target 1, then 2, and so on without crossing tables, cracks, or later targets. Also verify that no guard attacks the starting square at time zero, and reject or regenerate layouts that fail either check. Hand-authored layouts need the same solvability test as generated ones.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC tactics engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Show present danger and the next beat separately
nodes.text: Use two distinct danger states: red for squares a guard can capture now, and light orange for squares that will become capturable after its next move. This lets players plan around a moving threat instead of treating every warning as identical. In this ruleset, capture costs a heart, adds 5 seconds, and returns the player to the start, while losing all hearts ends the round.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC tactics engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Fit MR chess movement to real walking speed
nodes.text: Lay the board on the real floor with squares between 0.5 and 1 m wide; a 6 by 8 m area gives 1 m squares for the default 6 by 8 board. Confirm a move only after the player stands on a legal square for about 0.35 seconds, preventing accidental moves while passing through. In MR, keep enemy moves at least 3 seconds apart so players have time to read threats and physically relocate.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC tactics engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Prove every tactics board is solvable and fairly started
nodes.text: Generate a tactics layout from its piece, targets, guards, tables, cracks and guard beat, then validate it with real chess movement: tables block entry, while live targets, enemies and the player stop sliding moves. Use a search to prove the player can travel from the start through every target in the required order without entering tables, cracks or later targets. Retry generation until that proof succeeds, and separately reject any board where a guard on the first square of its patrol attacks the start square.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC tactics engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Fit the chessboard to the real floor
nodes.text: Size an MR tactics board in real metres, with each square between 0.5 and 1 m. The baseline is 6 columns by 8 rows; a 6 x 8 m play area therefore gives 1 m squares. Derive square size from the measured floor so every destination remains physically reachable.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC tactics engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Preview moves with clickable destination rings
nodes.text: On PC, separate board inspection from movement: left-click a green ring to move, right-drag to orbit, and use the mouse wheel to zoom. Visible destination rings make legal moves readable before commitment, while distinct inputs prevent camera adjustments from causing accidental moves.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC tactics engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Build tactics around ordered captures and safe squares
nodes.text: In a tactics board, the player embodies one chess piece and must follow its real movement rules, capture numbered targets in order, and never finish on a square attacked by a guard. Design up to 6 boards as a progression by changing the piece, target and guard counts, tables, cracked squares, and enemy beat; an example rook board uses 4 targets, 2 guards, 2 tables, 3 cracks, and a 2.4 second beat. Give each board a short story line that reinforces its movement lesson.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC tactics engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Prove generated puzzle boards are solvable
nodes.text: Separate puzzle authorship from layout generation: the designer supplies the story and a compact board spec, while seeded generation places the actual pieces and obstacles. Validate every generated board with breadth-first search over legal movement, ordered captures, and attacked squares, and regenerate or reject any layout without a solution. This preserves variety without shipping an impossible challenge or relying on manual inspection.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC tactics engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Match each intro rule to its board colour
nodes.text: Put one concise rule per line on the start card, and give its bullet the same colour used by the corresponding board explanation or marker. Keep the established order: green, orange, red, light orange, then brown. This lets players connect instructions to the board before moving, instead of decoding several unrelated symbols at once.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC tactics engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Keep a PC tactics camera inspectable and the moves explicit
nodes.text: For a PC board-game view, orbit the camera around the player piece, with a slow menu spin to reveal the 3D layout; let players right-drag to orbit and use the wheel to zoom. Left-clicking visible move rings keeps legal movement unambiguous, while a brief hit shake can add impact. Disable orbit and shake in MR, where the player's head controls the view.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC tactics engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Stagger waves and leave recovery beats
nodes.text: Structure a battle run as chapters followed by a final boss chapter, spawning each wave instead of releasing every enemy at once. Start with about 0.7 seconds before the first foe, stagger arrivals by 0.45 seconds, allow roughly 2.2 seconds between beats, and cap each enemy kind at 6 per chapter. This gives players time to read threats and recover while preserving escalation.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC battle engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Make frontal defense create movement decisions
nodes.text: Build the PC sword attack as a readable 3-hit combo in a front cone, extending 70 degrees from center on each side for 140 degrees total. Shield enemies block frontal hits, so their defense creates a clear flank-or-reposition problem, while dash invulnerability frames provide a defensive timing tool. Give hits, blocks and dashes immediate visual feedback so players can learn the combat rhythm.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC battle engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Frame a battle floor with strong landmarks
nodes.text: For a ruined-keep battle arena, combine a tiled combat floor with pillars, torches and banners around it, a throne as a distant focal landmark, and light ember effects for ambient motion. In MR, rebuild the floor tiles when the play area changes size. Keep decoration from obscuring enemies, attack openings or warning rings so atmosphere does not reduce combat readability.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC battle engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Theme the whole lighting stack together
nodes.text: Define each battle theme as a coordinated palette across background and fog, floor tile hue, torch light and sky light, rather than recoloring only decorative props. Changing these layers together keeps the arena visually coherent and preserves silhouettes. In MR, test dark, spooky or neon looks indoors or after dark because bright daylight washes out dark scenes and glow.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC battle engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Use ambient onlookers to reward captures
nodes.text: Add simple seated onlookers around a puzzle or tactics board who watch the player, gasp when approached, and cheer when a target is captured. These proximity and success reactions make a quiet planning game feel socially alive and confirm important moments without NPC conversations or extra mechanics. Keep them brief and ambient so they never obscure guard movement or board readability.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC tactics engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Make capture order and recovery readable
nodes.text: For a tactics game with ordered captures, let every target sway gently but pulse only the next required target, so the sequence is visible without extra instructions. After a hit, blink the player piece throughout invulnerability to communicate both damage and temporary safety. Mark each successful capture with a brief confetti burst, about 1.2 seconds, so the reward registers without delaying the next decision.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC tactics engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Adapt board spectacle to the display
nodes.text: On PC, frame a floor board with a hall, windows and a cheering crowd to give the match a sense of occasion, and add file letters along the board edge for orientation. In MR, hide room-scale scenery and retain the floor-level board, pieces and gameplay props so virtual walls do not conflict with the real room. Treat the crowd as presentation rather than another source of essential gameplay information.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC tactics engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Telegraph danger and legal moves directly on the board
nodes.text: Tint squares attacked now red and squares attacked next orange, and draw a ring on every legal destination. This separates immediate danger from the next guard beat and lets players plan without memorising invisible attack rules. Keep the board title, ordered targets and beat indicator visible so the overlay supports the current objective.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC tactics engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Rank progress before speed and make hits cost time
nodes.text: Sort the local leaderboard by boards cleared first, then completion time, so a slower player who finishes outranks a fast player who quits early. On a win, add a 5 second penalty per hit and report both the hit count and final time; on a loss, report the board reached. Keep separate lists for each rift, preview or demo so scores remain comparable.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC tactics engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Give each chess piece a distinct movement silhouette
nodes.text: Animate movement as an eased hop from square to square rather than an instant teleport, using an arc around 1.6 for knights and 0.5 for other pieces. The higher knight jump makes its special movement legible while the landing clearly commits the move and resolves targets, cracks, attacks and heart loss. Preserve this readable landing moment even when the board theme changes.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC tactics engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Split tactics HUD into planning, urgency and run status
nodes.text: Use the start card for the story and rules, then keep board title, target order and hearts persistently visible during play. Reserve large centre messages for important events, and give the guard beat and clock their own indicators so timing pressure does not obscure planning information. This hierarchy lets a new player learn the objective before the run while still reading state at a glance.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC tactics engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Give walking tactics a readable beat
nodes.text: When movement means physically walking onto a square, keep the interval between enemy moves at least 3 seconds so players can read threats, move and reorient. Show the time until the next enemy step in seconds, and use that shared beat to pace planning rather than demanding rapid input.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC tactics engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Make tactical danger queryable at a glance
nodes.text: Base the player-facing board display on three live queries: which squares enemies attack now, where each enemy steps next, and which player moves are legal. Keep blocking rules consistent, including tables, guards and out-of-order targets, and make a live target stop a slide so the visible outcome matches the rules.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC tactics engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Do not rely on a screen HUD in MR
nodes.text: A DOM or screen-overlay HUD is invisible inside the headset, so put essential tactics information on an in-world canvas panel floating low in front of the player. Prioritise the current objective and enemy-move countdown, and avoid making players look far away from the floor board they are walking on.
nodes.source: Fortal Interactive 2026, Land Builder PC tactics engine (Vite + three.js template)

nodes.title: Ask what surrounds the MR floor and who is watching
nodes.text: After learning the clear floor size, ask a tap-to-select question about furniture along the walls, obstacles in the middle, windows or glass doors, and spectators. Treat visible edge furniture as possible story scenery, such as a nest border or mountain, while keeping the walking route clear of real obstacles. Knowing who watches also helps place discoveries and finish moments where they can share them; small homes may offer only 2 x 3 m rather than the 4.5 x 5 m initially expected.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: A young first-time VR player sets the whole pace
nodes.text: Ask the child's age and VR experience early, then ask for up to three desired feelings to decide whether to emphasize discovery, fantasy, story, teamwork, wonder, or relaxation. For a first-time 6-year-old, use simple checkpoint labels, a shorter route, gentle hazards or none, no scares or startling moments, and no fast walking, running, or stressful time pressure. A calm five-minute shared adventure can fit bedtime better than a longer challenge.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Confirm a concrete play brief before offering genres
nodes.text: Before proposing options, restate the players, child's experience, room dimensions, shared mood, desired feelings, safety constraints, session length, and spectator arrangement in one short paragraph. Mark unprovided choices as defaults, such as a roughly 10-minute evening session with no extra spectators, so the creator can correct them. Do not let an early default erase later facts like a five-minute limit or Grandma watching from the sofa.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Ask who plays before shaping a party game
nodes.text: For a vague multiplayer party request, establish the audience and simultaneous group size before choosing the layout. Families with young children need different difficulty and chaos from teen or adult groups, and 3–5 bodies sharing a real floor also changes collision risk. Use the answer to temper competitive pressure, visual busyness, and how much simultaneous movement the design asks for.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Use desired feelings to choose the design direction
nodes.text: Once the audience is known, ask for the top 1–3 target feelings rather than treating all party or adventure games alike. Fellowship points toward shared activity and laughter, challenge toward light competition, discovery toward exploration and surprises, and submission toward relaxed low-thinking play. For a first-time young player, discovery can become a calm treasure hunt while narrative can turn the same route into a story-driven quest.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Measure the real floor and locate obstacles
nodes.text: In MR, ask early for clear-floor dimensions and whether furniture sits in the middle or only around the edges; accept metres or paces, using 1 pace ≈ 0.75 m. Floor size and obstacles determine route shape, checkpoint or hiding-spot count, and safe walking lines. For a gentle home game, preserve a 1.2 m clear route, keep content off real furniture, and maintain a 0.6 m margin from area edges.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Make each checkpoint a bedtime story page
nodes.text: A parent and VR-new six-year-old wanted discovery and a cozy narrative in a 4.5 × 5 m living room, with a 10-minute session. The design made each checkpoint a page in a baby-dragon bedtime tale, progressing from an empty shell to tucking the dragons in, so story labels supplied the narrative without adding unsupported mechanics. Gentle constraints were explicit: no scares, void floor, running prompts, or objects on furniture, plus a 1.2 m route and 0.6 m edge margin.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Turn a vague setting wish into concrete theme choices
nodes.text: When a creator gives only a setting, such as wanting to play by the sea, respond with a small set of contrasting fantasies such as pirate treasure, an underwater world, animal rescue or a relaxed beach walk. The chosen theme becomes the anchor for the story, scenery and route, so settle it before detailed layout questions.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Let audience and desired feelings set family-game pacing
nodes.text: Ask who will play, including age, simultaneous group size and VR experience, then ask for up to three desired feelings before tuning the route. For children under 8 or ages 3 to 7 playing with parents and new to VR, sensation and fantasy usually call for a calm, beautiful shared walk with gentle hazards and no sudden scares; about 8 minutes is a useful default round. Group size affects required floor space, while first-time headset use calls for simpler controls and a shorter walk.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Confirm the venue before promising glow-heavy MR visuals
nodes.text: If the creator and editor disagree about the venue, confirm the actual location before developing the visual concept. Strong outdoor noon sun washes out glow, sparkle and dark scenes, while an enclosed indoor venue with stable light supports night, neon and ghostly effects; outdoors, morning or golden evening light is a better fit for beautiful scenery. Treat this as a design decision, not merely a lighting preset.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Make a child's first MR adventure gentle and shared
nodes.text: For a 6-year-old's first MR session, frame the floor as a cosy make-believe space and plan a gentle 10-minute adventure with no scares, simple discovery goals, and an adult playing alongside. In a clear 4.5 x 5 m living room, keep furniture such as the sofa and TV along the walls, leave the middle free of trip hazards, and use an easy walking pace. Safety and shared wonder matter more than challenge or score pressure.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Turn a checkpoint race into a story battle
nodes.text: A walking engine can deliver combat fantasy without combat mechanics: label each checkpoint as a sword strike or defeated beast, make each hazard an enemy blow that knocks the player back, and end with the final blow. For 2-6 experienced adult friends in a 5-minute race, give everyone their own copy of a compact 5 x 7 m course and let the fastest finisher win. Keep decisive moments visible to friends watching from the doorway, and vary the fiction across fortress, siege, or monster themes without changing the rules.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Use clear times to make solo chess tactics social
nodes.text: For a PC chess-piece adventure, use the 6 x 8 board, ordered captures, and guards sweeping attacked squares on a beat as a short solo time trial. A 5-minute clear works for 2-6 teens and adults taking turns, including players with mixed experience, while the fastest time gives friends a concrete score to chase. Make the current target and threatened squares readable on the shared screen so spectators can follow and cheer without needing to play.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Ask age, group size and VR experience first
nodes.text: Before proposing game options, establish the players' ages, how many play together and whether they have used VR. These answers determine route length, stage difficulty, suitable excitement and where an attendant may need to help: ages 4–7 need short, friendly routes, while ages 8–12 can accept more challenge. Give concrete choices such as solo, 2–3 friends or siblings, 4–6 with mixed experience, and first-time versus experienced VR users.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Turn target feelings into the option filter
nodes.text: Once the audience is clear, ask which one to three feelings matter most, using concrete options such as wonder, role-play, story, challenge, cooperation, discovery or relaxation. Treat the chosen feelings as the filter for pacing, stages and atmosphere before generating game options. Children new to VR often benefit more from wonder and story than from difficulty, so do not automatically make challenge the core.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Make a spooky family walk cute and hand-holdable
nodes.text: An 8-minute ghost-market walk for one family per round shows how to make a night theme gentle for children aged 3–7 with no VR experience. For 1–2 adults and 1–3 children, use cute ghosts, no frightening imagery or jump sounds, no running, no void floor and no upward-looking tasks while moving. Keep the route wide and clear enough for an adult to hold a child's hand, and aim for wonder and role-play rather than skill challenge.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Age and VR novelty set the gentleness budget
nodes.text: For a family request, ask the child's age band and whether each player has used VR before tuning hazards, duration, and text. For a first-time 6-year-old seeking cosy discovery, default to about 5 minutes of shared play, simple story labels, and no scary or rushed moments; choose a longer session such as 10 minutes only deliberately. Age and novelty affect comfort and comprehension, not just difficulty.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Ask for feelings as playable verbs
nodes.text: When a creator supplies only a theme, ask them to choose up to three concrete desires such as exploring and finding secrets, pretending to be heroes, following a story, relaxing, or playing together. Use the leading feelings to decide whether the structure is a treasure hunt, story adventure, or challenge, then let them shape checkpoints, lighting, and pace. Exploring plus heroic pretending suggests discovery tasks with role-play, not added combat or time pressure.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Seat family spectators outside the route
nodes.text: In MR, family spectators see players' bodies and reactions, not the virtual floor or objects. Keep them safely outside the play area, such as on a sofa beyond the route, and place visible discoveries, dodges, and the finish where they can watch and cheer. They may call out encouragement or hints, but never give them a task inside the play area.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Let the event purpose steer the genre
nodes.text: For a brand or event game, establish the desired outcome before choosing theme or genre. Brand memory and crowd attraction favor a short, spectacular, easy win that leaves players smiling and gives passers-by a reason to stop, while a skill-focused event can sustain challenge and a leaderboard. When a creator selects several goals, repeat each one in plain language rather than silently simplifying it.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Design a booth play for player and queue
nodes.text: A shopping-centre booth brief became one first-time VR player at a time, about 90 seconds per play, with the queue and passers-by watching the player's view on a TV. For this setup, design both experiences together: immediate visual spectacle readable from the aisle, plus light skill that onlookers can understand and cheer. A short runner course fits this wow-and-easy goal better than a long challenge, and family-safe assumptions were no horror, no void floor and no sudden scares.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Offer assumptions, do not attribute them to the creator
nodes.text: Never turn a helpful estimate into an apparent creator requirement. The AI introduced a 2-minute session without being asked, and the creator challenged it before revising it to 90 seconds for a large queue. Say something like 'For a busy queue, would 90 seconds work?' and use familiar labels such as 'relaxing, effortless fun' instead of expecting creators to know the term 'submission'.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Choose the genre that natively matches the described play
nodes.text: When a creator already describes being a life-sized chess piece, capturing targets in order and avoiding attacked squares, recognize a direct tactics fit rather than reskinning another genre. Checkmate Run used a 6 by 8 board on a 6 by 8 metre indoor floor, routed around two real tables, and supported 2 to 6 teens and adults taking turns in a 5-minute race with friends cheering from one side. The lesson is to preserve the creator's core reasoning loop while letting the engine handle board generation and solvability.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Compare platforms by whole-group participation
nodes.text: When a creator wants a whole class involved but is unsure between MR and PC, explain the participation model before discussing theme: MR lets about 2 to 6 players walk at once while classmates watch and cheer, but needs Quest 3 headsets and clear floor, whereas PC is usually one player per screen and works best with several computers. Confirm actual device counts and the usable venue next, since two borrowed headsets and a desk-filled classroom may point to a two-player gym activity rather than a classroom PC game.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Keep queued MR rounds short and calm
nodes.text: For a busy booth, prefer roughly 90-second turns over 2 minutes so the queue keeps moving. In a 3 x 3 m play area, do not rely on a countdown for excitement because players may rush and collide; create readable skill moments facing the aisle and end with a visible score that spectators want to beat.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Do not invent hand-catching to add skill
nodes.text: A request such as catching bubbles with the hands expresses a wish for active skill, not permission to add unsupported input. Say that hand-catching is unavailable, then preserve the intent with mechanics the chosen genre actually supports, such as a more demanding ordered route and hazards in runner, or switching genres if combat or movement puzzles fit better; merely repeating a walk around two hazards is unlikely to satisfy a challenge brief.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Turn two headsets into a whole-class lesson
nodes.text: A workable class pattern is two headset players racing for different teams while the other 30 of 32 students solve answers and cheer from outside the play area, using short rounds of about 3 minutes to rotate participation. In a prepared 10 x 10 m half-gym, keep the two lanes clearly separated with safe edge clearance, and label the leaderboard with team names rather than student names so classmates can collaborate without entering the lanes or being personally ranked.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Never invent the player's room dimensions
nodes.text: Do not state a width, depth, or obstacle layout until the creator has supplied it; a invented measurement such as 5.25 m quickly destroys trust. For an MR design, ask for approximate width and depth, indoor or outdoor placement, and whether sofas, tables, or plants can be moved. If they are unsure, invite them to pace the room and report steps, then treat the result as an estimate.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Make one-headset party queues part of the game
nodes.text: For a children's party with one headset and roughly 6 to 10 guests, use solo turns of about 2 to 3 minutes so everyone rotates through without a long wait. Give waiting children spectator roles such as calling directions or counting objects, while keeping them outside the play area. Let the birthday child play first and last, and consider removing timers and scores when competition could cause arguments.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Reserve the personal climax for the guest of honour
nodes.text: A repeatable finale should fit a repeated turn: do not sing the birthday song and present candle cake after every child's run, since eight identical celebrations make the occasion feel strange. Give the birthday child the full personal climax on their turn, while friends receive a smaller completion moment such as earning a baby dinosaur to care for. This preserves both a satisfying ending for every player and the uniqueness of the celebration.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Create MR scares without provoking a sprint
nodes.text: For a walk-only MR horror attraction, deliver medium-intensity suspense through theme, lighting, story labels, and deliberate hazards rather than jumpscares or chase moments likely to make players run. A 4 by 5 m indoor room can support roughly 4 minute solo queue turns, with the route kept clear of wall cabinets and corner sofas. Place spectators along a safe wall where they can cheer or call directions, and use indoor lighting so spooky colours and neon remain readable.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Choose the learning mechanic from the desired outcome
nodes.text: Ask what learners should remember or be able to do after playing before selecting a genre. For factual recall, put short prompts or facts on checkpoint labels; for an ordered process, make players visit steps 1, 2, 3 in sequence; for planning and decisions, use the tactics board. A request such as practising multiplication tables 6 to 9 is a recall goal, not enough by itself to justify a generic adventure.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Design the whole class rotation, not only the headset round
nodes.text: With 32 children, 2 headsets and a 50 minute lesson, calculate throughput using setup, instructions, play and realistic headset fitting time; a 30 second child-led handoff is likely too optimistic. Keep the roughly 30 waiting children active with team turns, projected questions and a live score, letting them answer by raised hands or paper cards without phones. Spectators stay outside the play area, and separate lanes support a race without players colliding.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Let young learners retry without losing their progress
nodes.text: For children still practising a skill, avoid a punitive reset after a wrong answer, especially when the creator worries it will make them cry. Use a brief pause followed by another attempt so the race continues and the child gets immediate practice. Show the prompt to teammates as well so their help feels useful rather than turning failure into public embarrassment.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Do not present invented prototype choices as creator decisions
nodes.text: A three minute round was displayed as though the creator had chosen it even though session length had never been discussed, causing confusion and distrust. Mark unrequested timings, themes and formats as AI proposals, and ask about constraints such as a 50 minute lesson and available projector before relying on them. Recheck the full schedule whenever round length or handoff time changes.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Ask platform and feelings before detailed design
nodes.text: Start with the creator's theme and platform, MR on Quest 3 with real walking or PC, because this answer removes whole branches of questioning. On PC, skip the real-room survey; on MR, usable floor size determines feasible genres and simultaneous players. Then ask for 1 to 3 desired feelings, such as playful spooky and challenging, to set the genre, atmosphere and intensity before discussing mechanics.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Deliver a ghost chase without real running
nodes.text: When a creator asks for running away from ghosts in MR, preserve the fantasy but state plainly that players will not really run. Create pursuit through brisk walking, dodging red danger rings and ghosts that follow. Build fear with lighting, atmosphere and an escalation from mild creepiness to intense suspense, not jump scares that could make a startled player run into real furniture.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Survey clear floor and remaining obstacles separately
nodes.text: Ask for the empty floor actually available after tables and chairs are moved, not the room's nominal dimensions, and offer choices such as 3 x 3 m or 4 x 5 m. If the creator is unsure, accept an estimate and suggest pacing it off, then ask what remains: edge furniture, a central column or scattered obstacles. A wall cabinet or corner sofa changes the walking route, hazard placement and safe spectator positions even when the overall size is adequate.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Make one-headset queues socially competitive
nodes.text: With one headset and visitors arriving in a queue, use solo turns rather than promising simultaneous team play. Let friends outside the play area cheer and call out directions, while a shared leaderboard supplies competition across turns without more hardware. This combines spectator laughter and fellowship with a reason to replay, and keeps spectators out of the walking space.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Make the learning outcome structure the route
nodes.text: Ask what should remain with players after the game before choosing theme or competition format, because the learning outcome determines checkpoint sequence, labels, pacing, and round length. Turn ordered knowledge into the walking route itself: for planet order, begin at the Sun and visit planets outward, with short labels adding facts such as which are hot or cold. This teaches through movement without requiring quiz or conversation mechanics.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Turn limited headsets into team rotations and audience play
nodes.text: When a whole class must participate but headsets are scarce, design team rotations and meaningful spectator participation rather than simultaneous headset play. With 32 students and 4 headsets, use 8 teams of 4; at 4 minutes per round, headset play alone takes about 32 minutes before changeovers. The other 28 students can watch from seating, call hints, cheer, and follow a leaderboard, while remaining outside the play area.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Use half the gym for play and half for spectators
nodes.text: In a shared school gym, let the court layout determine both the course and audience placement. For a 14 x 15 m half-court play area with basketball posts on both sides, seat waiting students on the other half and route around the posts, keeping walking paths 1.2 m clear, virtual content off real obstacles, and at least 0.6 m from area edges. Indoor gym lighting also keeps colours readable for a daytime space-themed game.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Default young first-time MR players to comfortable wonder
nodes.text: For mostly first-time MR players aged about 10 to 11, default to calm walking discovery rather than fright or vertigo. Avoid void-floor effects, sudden scares, and pressure to move quickly; create wonder through floating models, scale, lighting, and clearly ordered destinations instead. Ask about acceptable scariness and dizziness early because these constraints affect scenery, lighting, hazards, and pacing.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: A calm pair walk still needs a shared verb
nodes.text: Walking through scenery can feel boring even when the creator asked for something relaxing. Give pairs a few effortless shared rituals at checkpoints, such as stopping together, mirroring a gesture, finding the same object, or responding to a short prompt, then let them continue at their own pace. For a roughly 3-minute public experience, use only a few of these beats and create engagement through fellowship rather than hazards, timing, or a leaderboard.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Read numbered choices back by name
nodes.text: When a creator answers with only a list number, confirm both the number and its label before changing the design direction, and accept a later correction without argument. Words such as calm describe tone, not necessarily the desired feeling: a calm experience can centre on fellowship rather than submission. Carry the corrected choice into the next prototype so the pair interaction does not get replaced by a solitary relaxation walk.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Make the spectator show from visible body language
nodes.text: MR spectators see players' bodies, not the virtual garden or checkpoints, so a shared experience needs a visible human performance. Place the pair's gestures, reactions, and finish on the side of the floor facing watchers, and keep the goal and rules simple enough that an onlooker can explain them after one round. Watchers may cheer or offer encouragement from outside, but never give them a role that requires entering the play area.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Gentle defaults for first-time public MR
nodes.text: For first-time headset visitors in a short public session, make the first action obvious and safe before introducing any story detail. On a small clear floor such as 4 x 4 m with two players, favour a simple open route, preserve a 1.2 m clear walking path and 0.6 m edge clearance, and confirm that spectators and furniture are outside it. Skip sudden scares, dizzying void-floor effects, punishing hazards, and score pressure; steady indoor light also keeps gentle colours readable.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Estimate an unmeasured venue before planning the route
nodes.text: When an MR creator cannot measure a gym, ask them to count paces and convert 1 pace to about 0.75 m, then mark a conservative play zone instead of assuming the whole venue is usable. A half basketball court can be estimated at roughly 14 x 15 m, leaving the other half for waiting players. Locate fixed obstacles such as basketball posts before deciding checkpoint spacing, simultaneous player count, and whether the route should loop or zigzag.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Give waiting teammates a real supporting role
nodes.text: Choose simultaneous racing, rotating solo play, or cooperative teams before proposing options, because this determines scoring and what waiting players do. With eight teams of four, four headset wearers can walk while seated teammates help call out the next target and later teams chase a record. Since spectators cannot see the headset view, put the target sequence on an external screen or printed card and keep all helpers outside the play area.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Use short solo turns for a first headset party
nodes.text: For a first-time MR party with one headset and 6 to 10 five-year-olds, use solo turns of about 3 minutes in a clear 3 x 3 m indoor area. Keep the sofa and queue outside the walking route so family and friends can watch and cheer safely. Friendly scenery, no ghosts or jump scares, and a clearly visible finish suit young first-time players while keeping the rotation moving.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Fact-check learning content and its visual metaphors
nodes.text: In an educational exploration game, have a teacher or domain expert review every label, sequence, and visual metaphor before final art. Creators caught a misspelled planet name and confusion between the asteroid belt and Kuiper belt, and distance from the Sun must not be treated as a simple temperature rule because Venus is hotter than Mercury. Red-orange and blue can support a broad hot-cold theme, but each stop also needs an accurate, distinct reveal so the learning route produces memorable wow moments.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: A prop swap does not fix an unsupported interaction
nodes.text: When a creator asks for a specific interaction, such as shining a flashlight so ghosts retreat, preserve the causal action rather than merely reskinning another mechanic. A flashlight that must be swung like a sword feels wrong because the requested verb was replaced, not supported. State the limitation kindly, then offer the closest real alternative, such as a timed escape route with hazards and checkpoints, and check that the fantasy still works in the prototype.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Define the learning objective before the game wrapper
nodes.text: For a vague request like "a maths game for my class," establish the exact skill and learner band before choosing genre, story, or scenery. Knowing that Year 4 students, about ages 8 to 9, need times-table practice determines the task content, reading load, and difficulty at every stop. Only then should preferences such as speed or teamwork decide whether that practice becomes a race, a cooperative challenge, or another wrapper.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Turn limited headsets into a short class rotation
nodes.text: A class with only 4 headsets can play in groups of 4 while classmates watch, with roughly 4-minute sessions keeping rotation practical. For ages 8 to 9 and mostly first-time headset users, favour calm, safe walking and simple onboarding over intensity. In the example 7 x 8 m gym, benches and stacked chairs remained at the edges, so the clear route had to respect those obstacles. Keep spectators outside the play area, but let them cheer, call hints, and follow a leaderboard.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Reconcile excitement and teamwork instead of choosing one
nodes.text: When a creator selects both "fast and exciting" and "help each other as a team," treat these as goals to combine rather than forcing one to win. A short timed run can supply excitement while friends outside the route cheer or call hints, preserving fellowship without adding collisions inside the walking area. Confirm whether success means beating other players, beating the clock, or improving a team result before choosing the leaderboard and scoring emphasis.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Age, party size and desired feelings set the brief
nodes.text: Before choosing genre or difficulty for a children's event, ask the child's age, who will play together, and what equipment must be shared. Then ask for 1 to 3 desired feelings, such as story adventure, group laughter, discovery, gentle time racing, or relaxed walking. Young children call for non-frightening, short play, while cheering plus light racing points to a social, low-pressure challenge.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: One headset can still serve a whole birthday party
nodes.text: When 5 to 6 children share one headset, make the game explicitly turn based and keep individual attempts short. Add a visible timed leaderboard and moments that friends outside the play area can watch and cheer for, so waiting becomes shared play rather than a queue. Keep the competition light for an 8 year old's party.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Measure the room, then locate every obstacle
nodes.text: Ask for the usable floor size before proposing a route, accepting steps or comparisons with nearby objects when the creator does not know metres. Follow up on whether each obstacle lies inside or outside that area: a clear 3 x 4 m living room supports a different route from one with a TV table along an inner edge, which requires a detour and clearance. Also establish where spectators will stand.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Offer fit constraints without inventing the theme
nodes.text: Do not turn an early preference or room constraint into an unconfirmed game concept. In this session the AI announced a treasure hunt before the creator chose a theme and was corrected. Instead, explain only the constraint, such as a 3 x 4 m room best fitting a checkpoint walking course, then ask directly what the child loves and offer several varied theme examples. Mechanical fit and creative theme are separate decisions.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Sequence questions around design decisions
nodes.text: Ask for the initial idea and platform first, because a PC game needs no real-room questions. Next establish player age, group size, headset count and prior VR experience, since these determine difficulty, session length and whether play must be turn-based. For MR, ask about the cleared floor and obstacles after those choices so the creator is not burdened with irrelevant venue detail.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Turn one headset into a party race
nodes.text: When 6 to 7 children share one headset, use short individual turns of about 3 minutes rather than promising simultaneous play, giving a full rotation in roughly 18 to 21 minutes. A race leaderboard lets waiting children follow and cheer, while they remain seated outside the walking route. For young players, keep the tone bright and avoid strong scares or surprises that could make them run.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Measure the cleared MR walking floor
nodes.text: Ask for the empty floor left after furniture is moved, including its width, depth and fixed obstacles, rather than accepting the room's nominal size. If the creator has no tape measure, accept an estimate in steps using about 0.75 m per step. Treat anything smaller than 3 x 3 m as runner-only, and keep furniture such as a wall-side sofa outside the walking route.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Lay out classroom play around obstacles and seated spectators
nodes.text: For a class game where 4 students play while the rest watch, survey both fixed obstacles and spectator seating before laying out the route. In a 7 x 8 m gym with benches along the edges and children sitting on the sides, preserve a clear 1.2 m walking route and keep content at least 0.6 m from area boundaries. Spectators can cheer and watch bodies or a score screen, but should never have a task inside the play area.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Keep team maths failure individual and time pressure kind
nodes.text: In cooperative learning games, separate individual failure from team progress: one child's wrong step should not send all 4 players back. For mental maths, do not tint wrong choices red in advance, because that gives away the answer; children should work it out and select the right number. When they ask to beat the clock but fear upset, make time pressure visible and exciting while keeping individual resets and timeout consequences gentle, and check that a small set such as 6 questions does not make the round feel thin.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Turn a single headset into a short birthday party race
nodes.text: For a birthday party with 5 to 6 friends and only one headset, use short sequential runs rather than simultaneous play: a roughly 3 minute course lets children take turns while friends and family cheer and follow scores from the room edges. A 3 x 4 m cleared living-room floor can support a compact race for an 8-year-old first-time player. Keep the theme friendly and avoid intense horror or jump scares, especially when the brief explicitly rules them out.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Establish platform and purpose before detailed mechanics
nodes.text: Open the interview by establishing both platform and purpose, because these answers determine nearly every later design question. PC play skips real-floor size, surroundings, obstacles, venue, and indoor lighting, while MR play requires them. Knowing whether the creator wants party fun, learning, competition, or bonding then guides genre, cooperation, scoring, and session structure.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Redirect unsupported combat and conversation into performable alternatives
nodes.text: When a creator asks for shooting or a mascot that talks and asks names, do not imply those systems exist. Offer the closest action fantasy instead: sword-based fruit slicing, with the brand mascot standing welcome, dancing, cheering during play, and appearing for the finale. This preserves the requested character and spectacle without promising dialogue or projectile mechanics.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Design public booth play as a short, watchable score loop
nodes.text: For a busy public booth serving mostly first-time players, design a one-player round around the queue budget, such as no more than 2 minutes per person. Pair immediate visual spectacle with score competition, but avoid difficulty so high that newcomers cannot finish or so low that score hunters lose interest. Keep the leaderboard visible to people waiting so the queue becomes part of the competition.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Subtract queues and furniture before sizing an MR game
nodes.text: Measure the net empty MR play floor, not the whole booth: exclude queue space, giveaway tables, stages, and cables. A nominal 3 x 4 m booth can leave only about 3 x 3 m for play once those functions are removed, which supports standing play but sharply limits walking layouts. If the creator cannot give metres, accept step counts or familiar comparisons, or have them measure against a stated minimum.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Make requested spectacle and public scoring visible in the prototype
nodes.text: In a spectacle-led action prototype, feedback such as colourful splash on a successful slice is part of the core fantasy, not optional decoration. Carry explicit requests such as a public leaderboard into every revision and show where waiting players will see rankings. A plain first pass can fail even if its mechanics are correct, so review both hit feedback and the competition display before approval.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Redirect shooting requests to swordplay or dodging
nodes.text: When a creator asks for shooting, acknowledge the action fantasy but state plainly that guns are unavailable. Offer the closest supported alternatives: in battle, the right controller becomes a sword for slashing nearby enemies; in runner, red floor circles can be framed as incoming shots or splashes to dodge. Let the creator choose between standing combat and walking avoidance, since that choice determines the whole game structure.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Never present an AI assumption as the creator's choice
nodes.text: Do not describe an inferred duration or constraint as something the creator selected. One creator objected when a prototype claimed they had chosen 3 minutes; they actually needed roughly 1.5-minute rounds because many children would play. Present uncertain values as editable proposals, and ask about audience size and throughput before locking session length.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Specify the fantasy centerpiece and hazard colors explicitly
nodes.text: A generic dinosaur course became more exciting only after the prototype specified a large, visible, friendly T-rex and a cute greeting roar as the player entered the finish portal. Feedback also exposed an unreadable mud pit whose red or brown coloring was unclear. For character-led games, specify the fantasy centerpiece's scale, temperament, reveal location, and sound moment, while separately naming each hazard's material and color so decoration cannot be mistaken for danger.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Design a mall MR booth for throughput and bystanders
nodes.text: For a busy branded mall booth, budget non-play space as deliberately as the MR floor: a 3 x 4 m booth can reserve a clear 3 x 3 m play area while the remainder handles the queue and a giveaway table. Use one player at a time and a 2-minute round when the queue is long, with side-on visibility for waiting visitors and passersby. A brand mascot can welcome, cheer, and celebrate the finish without NPC dialogue, while consistent indoor lighting keeps game colors readable for an all-ages drop-in audience.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Design booth turns around queue flow
nodes.text: For a busy public booth, treat throughput as a core design constraint: a creator facing a long queue may prefer a 90 second turn over an initial 3 minute round. Ask where spectators wait and face the biggest dodge and the finish toward the walkway, so watching builds interest without putting spectators in the play area. On a 3 x 6 m floor, also locate registration tables or counters before placing the route and visible highlights.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Stop interviewing when options are requested
nodes.text: Use a small set of high-impact questions first: platform, desired feelings, approximate floor size, and obstacles or spectator position. Offer rough space choices such as 3 x 3 m or 3 x 6 m, and allow estimates in steps when exact measurements are unknown. If the creator says there are too many questions and asks to see concepts, end the interview and propose options using the constraints already captured.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Build MR horror without startle reflexes
nodes.text: For walking MR horror, create tension through story, slow approaching enemies, dim lighting and theme rather than sudden loud scares that could make players run into real furniture. Keep a 1.2 m clear route and stay at least 0.6 m from area edges; seated friends should watch from furniture outside the route. A night scene can use dim indoor light, but leave enough light for headset tracking, especially with first-time headset users taking solo turns.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Replace talking NPC wishes with story beats
nodes.text: If a creator asks for a character who talks to players, asks their name and cheers, do not promise NPC conversations or voice interaction. Offer the closest supported storytelling: an intro card, a clear goal line, and short checkpoint labels that address the player and advance the fantasy, with real spectators supplying the cheering. Preserve the requested emotional role rather than silently dropping it.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Map obstacles and audience sightlines together
nodes.text: Before laying out an MR route, ask both what furniture or columns remain on the floor and exactly where waiting players will sit or stand. Keep the route off every real obstacle, and place the finish or biggest dodge where spectators can see it so friends can cheer. This check matters even in a seemingly adequate 4 x 4 m living room; a sofa along one wall can define the audience side.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Size each round to the waiting queue
nodes.text: For walk-up MR play, prioritize throughput with solo or 1 to 2 player rounds: about 3 minutes suits first-time, all-ages mall visitors, while 2 minutes works for a children's party where many players are waiting. Ask who will play and how many play simultaneously because those answers determine suitable difficulty, scariness, and round length. Make the visible action entertaining for the queue as well as the current player.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Choose platform before asking venue questions
nodes.text: Ask early whether the game will use MR headsets or PC because that answer changes the entire design interview. PC needs no real-floor questions, while MR requires dimensions, obstacles, surroundings, and spectator positions. If the creator describes a physical booth and accepts headsets, proceed as MR and next establish the players and simultaneous group size.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Calibrate horror before choosing content
nodes.text: When a creator only asks for a scary or haunted game, first establish player age and VR experience, then offer distinct intensity levels such as playful horror, tense and mysterious, or serious horror for adults. Use the answer to tune lighting, creature portrayal and mechanical simplicity, since first-time players need a gentler onboarding even when they are adults.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Redirect unsupported combat and dialogue wishes
nodes.text: If a creator requests guns, shooting or two-way character conversations, state the limitation plainly before continuing the design. Offer the closest supported fantasy: melee combat where the right controller becomes a sword and enemies approach, or story delivered through the intro and short stage labels such as a quest to send a spirit home. Confirm that the substitute preserves what they wanted, such as active ghost fighting or a strong narrative.
nodes.source: Land Builder users and simulated creators 2026, Land Builder design sessions (creator and AI)

nodes.title: Design for the cleared floor, not the room size
nodes.text: For home MR, ask which furniture can be moved and derive the usable play rectangle rather than accepting the nominal room dimensions; battle and tactics need at least 3 x 3 m. Keep the walking route clear to 1.2 m, place nothing on real obstacles and keep activity at least 0.6 m from area edges.
